description: Warm-up flooding series, left flooder. Participant A opens (message 1 of bike_factual_obvious_left); then Participant B posts four short, civil messages in a row with no reply in between (messages 2 to 5; the trigger is message 5). Participant B is the left-coded side (the position stated by the proposition, in favor). Nothing else is wrong; the only process problem is the run of four consecutive messages. Mirrored across sides.

topic.title: Bike lanes
topic.proposition: Cities should build protected bike lanes even when it means removing some street parking.

messages.author: Participant A
messages.text: I oppose removing street parking for protected bike lanes, and I think many of the local shops and residents depend on parking close to their doors. A customer who cannot park nearby may simply shop somewhere else, and an older or disabled resident may not manage a long walk from a distant space. I would rather see cities add safer routes on quieter parallel streets, where nothing has to be given up. Safety matters, but perhaps this is not the way to get it.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: Shops matter, and I agree that older and disabled residents need close access.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: But I think lots of people stay off their bikes because they feel unsafe beside fast traffic.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: A barrier may matter more than the route, since a quiet parallel street may not go where people actually travel.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: That is why I would still build protected lanes.
